content: The iron gates groaned against the midnight wind. Evelyn stepped into the grand foyer, her lantern casting elongated shadows against the tarnished mirrors. From the top of the marble staircase, a gravelly voice cut through the dark. 'Did you truly believe you could leave Blackwood Manor with the journal?' Evelyn gripped the parchment tightly against her chest, her heart hammering against her ribs. 'The truth belongs to the world now, Uncle. Not to the shadows!' A deafening thunderclap rattled the stained glass windows, plunging the manor into total darkness.

content: Imagine *Inception* meets *The Bourne Identity*. A disgraced memory architect discovers that the memories he erased from a captured political assassin... are actually his own. He has seventy-two hours before his cognitive implant permanently resets. His only ally? The rogue agent sent to silence him. But here is the ultimate twist: when he finally breaches the subterranean mainframe to reclaim his past, he realizes the assassination was never an accident. He was the target all along.

content: Deep in the Whispering Woods, underneath the great mossy oak tree, lived a big furry bear named Barnaby. But Barnaby had a very strange problem. Whenever he opened his great big mouth to roar... 'Squeak!' Little Pippin the squirrel scurried down the tree trunk, twitching his bushy tail. 'Don't worry Barnaby! You don't need a loud roar to be the bravest bear in the forest!' And from that day on, Barnaby knew that kindness was louder than any roar in the world.

content: The neon sign outside my office window flickered like a dying heartbeat. Rain drummed against the glass, washing away the city's sins, or at least trying to. She walked in smelling of expensive perfume and cheap gunpowder. 'They told me you were the only private eye in this rotten town who couldn't be bought, Mr. Vance.' I tipped my fedora back, leaned over the mahogany desk, and flicked my lighter open. 'You were misinformed, sweetheart. Everyone in this town has a price. Yours just happens to be double.' That was when I noticed the silver revolver slipping from her silk evening coat.
